answer: Result handoff — full analysis executed. n.total semantics confirmed Case A (sum) in 632/632 rows. Three complementary metrics (prevalence, conditional share, abundance-weighted dominance) computed per habitat with B=5000 bootstrap CIs. Hurdle binomial model (Croplands reference) yields Wetlands OR=3.84 q=0.003, Urban OR=3.50 q=0.003, Coastal OR=3.12 q=0.019, Riparian OR=2.17 q=0.047 (all BH-FDR q<0.05). Env correlates (logit-LM z-scored + BH-FDR) identify elevation (OR=0.10 per SD, q=0.0008) and distance.road (OR=0.68 per SD, q=0.043) as mechanistic drivers. Phylogenetic Mantel-style K=0.957 p=0.004 kept supplementary. All artifacts saved under /workspace/artifacts/, analysis.py reproducible end-to-end.

payload.hypothesis: In the Catalonia study region, the prevalence of non-native plant species introduced via the gardening pathway varies steeply by habitat — it is highest in low-elevation, anthropogenically disturbed habitats close to roads and human settlements, peaking in Wetlands (50.0% of plots, 95% bootstrap CI 34.2–65.8%), Urban (47.7% [35.4–60.0%]), Coastal (44.8% [27.6–62.1%]), and Riparian (36.1% [24.6–47.5%]), and falling to near-zero in Rock outcrops (0%), Scrublands (1.9% [0.0–4.7%]), and forest interiors (Broad-leaved 4.4%, Coniferous 6.5%). Hurdle-binomial odds-ratios relative to the Croplands baseline (20.7% prevalence [12.0–29.3%]) are 3.84× for Wetlands, 3.50× for Urban, 3.12× for Coastal and 2.17× for Riparian (all BH-FDR q≤0.05); forests and Scrublands drop to 0.07–0.27× odds. The environmental gradient consistent with the ornamental-escape mechanism is dominated by elevation (odds ratio 0.10 per SD increase in elevation, q=0.0008) and proximity to roads (OR 0.68 per SD increase in distance-to-road, q=0.043), with the urban-vs-cropland buffer context collapsing to a non-significant PC1 once elevation is controlled. Stacked-composition analysis shows that when non-native species do occur they are dominated by gardening origin in lowland habitats (53–100% of non-native richness in Wetlands / Coastal / Coniferous / Broad-leaved forests) but not in Urban (29.8% gardening, 68.9% unintentional) or Croplands (18.5% gardening, 76.9% unintentional) where unintentional escape remains the leading driver. A supplementary phylogenetic-distance analysis suggests pathway categories are phylogenetically clustered (Mantel-style K=0.957, p=0.004, B=5000 permutations over 81 matched tips), but this does not drive the habitat-level hypothesis.
payload.workflow: Step 0 — n.total semantics: row-wise check that n.total == n.gard + n.unint + n.agfo (passed in 632/632 rows, Case A, so share_d == dominance_d). Step 1 — per-habitat prevalence, conditional share, and abundance-weighted dominance with B=5000 nonparametric bootstrap CIs at the plot level (low-n habitats flagged with explicit CIs). Step 2 — hurdle model with Croplands as reference: (a) binomial (logit) presence model with BH-FDR over 9 habitat coefficients (LLR p ≈ 4e-27, pseudo-R²=0.243); (b) zero-truncated Poisson count model (manual scipy implementation over n.gard>0, n=117 plots) with paired Poisson GLM with HC1 robust SE as a stability fallback (dispersion=1.14, Poisson adequate). Step 3 — env correlates: VIF check on 7 env predictors; PCA1 collapse of (urban.2009.500m, cropland.2009.500m) imposed (Urban=+0.84, Cropland=-0.55, 54% var) per protocol even though the VIF for that pair was ~1; remaining elevation/temperature/rainfall collinearity documented but not collapsed beyond protocol. Logit-LM on z-scored env predictors + BH-FDR q=0.05 across 9 coefs; joint habitat+env regularized logit (alpha=0.1) due to singular Hessian at full MLE. Step 4 — figure/data exports as CSV (matplotlib unavailable); ASCII bar visualisations embedded in ANALYSIS_REPORT.md. Step 5 — phylogenetic signal: custom Newick parser (biopython unavailable), 81/81 tips matched; K-clustering Mantel-style surrogate for Pagel's λ. Lazy confirmations: temporal_trends_contingency_table NOT used.
